generations.prompt:
An adult actor performs a scene on the practical bridge set of a warm, old-fashioned television space adventure, played with complete sincerity. The set is washed in soft red stage lighting.

The set gives a sudden theatrical shudder: the camera jolts and the seated Captain sways to one side and steadies himself with a hand on the arm of his chair. Behind him, out of focus, the officer braces on his console and a panel at the back of the set throws a brief shower of stage sparks. As the shaking settles, the Captain turns his head slightly toward the officer behind him and calls for a routine report, steady and calm. The Captain says: "Damage report." He faces forward again, mouth closed.

CAPTAIN VOICE: An older adult man with a low, resonant baritone, a lightly weathered dry texture, and clear, lightly British English. Measured, unhurried phrasing, precise consonants, restrained breath and quiet authority. Warmth lives underneath his composure. He speaks at an ordinary conversational volume, never booms, shouts, growls or delivers an impersonation. Preserve this same pitch, accent, timbre and cadence in every appearance.

Only the Captain speaks, and only that line. Sound: the spoken line exactly as written, a low rumble and rattle as the set shakes, one electrical crackle, the hum of the set. No music, no narration, no other voices, no added lines. No subtitles, captions or on-screen text.
